intent: procedure: sub-issue linking pattern for umbrella efforts
notes: **Extended `.gator/procedures/file-github-issue.md`** with the sub-issue linking pattern for umbrella efforts (e.g. "Gator Loop polish", "Enterprise post-MVP hardening"). Documents parent-issue conventions, child-issue conventions, and the `gh api` GraphQL mutation for linking sub-issues (there is no first-class `gh sub-issue` command yet, but the API is fully supported and works reliably via `gh api graphql -f query='mutation { addSubIssue(...) }'`).

**Notable GraphQL naming quirk captured**: the field is `subIssues` (plural, no `Connection` suffix), not `subIssuesConnection` as some GitHub docs suggest. Getting this wrong produces `Field 'subIssuesConnection' doesn't exist on type 'Issue'` — noted inline in the procedure so the next reader doesn't waste time.

**Demonstrated end-to-end on live repo**: filed [#5 Gator Loop polish (umbrella)](https://github.com/cumberland-laboratories/gator/issues/5) with three sub-issues (#6 Dashboard events timeline, #7 Dashboard session card, #8 Protocol refinement) — all linked via the mutation, all with Priority + Area=Loop + Status set on the board, parent shows `subIssuesSummary.total = 3, completed = 0` per GraphQL. Board view now has 8 items: the 4 standalone issues migrated 2026-08-04 (#1-#4) + the Loop umbrella + its 3 children.

**Roadmap categorization note**: the 4th roadmap item under "Building — Priority 2: Gator Loop Polish" ("Auto-trigger update after migration") is really Area=Packaging/Release, not Loop — v2.5.4's A4 fixed the vendor-hook half; the remaining gap (script content refresh after `--migrate-layout`) is a standalone migration polish. Draft body preserved at `.tmp/loop-sub4-auto-refresh-body.md` for filing as an independent issue with the correct area, not as a Loop sub-issue. The roadmap itself can move that row to Priority 1 (packaging/release polish) in a future roadmap edit.
Pattern is now reproducible: same procedure applies whenever a multi-surface effort needs a project-board umbrella (Enterprise post-MVP hardening is the natural next candidate).
